questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) The table shows the distribution of marks scored by 100 candidates in an examination.

| Mark ($x$) | 60 - 62 | 63 - 65 | 66 - 68 | 69 - 71 | 72 - 74 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Frequency ($f$) | 5 | 18 | 42 | 27 | 8 |

State the:

(a) number of classes or intervals in the distribution,
questions.corrige_markdown:
Count the class intervals: $60-62,\ 63-65,\ 66-68,\ 69-71,\ 72-74$.

**There are $5$ classes.**

The lower class limit is the smallest value written in the class.

**Lower class limit $=63$.**

The upper class limit is the largest value written in the class.

**Upper class limit $=74$.**

The modal class is the class with the highest frequency. The highest frequency is $42$.

**Modal class $=66-68$.**

The class mark is the middle value of the class: $\dfrac{60+62}{2}=61$.

**Class mark $=61$.**

questions.enonce_markdown: (f) class size of the distribution. *[10 marks for (i)]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The class size is the width of a class. Using class boundaries, the class $60-62$ runs from $59.5$ to $62.5$, so the size is $62.5-59.5=3$ (equivalently, the difference between two consecutive lower limits is $63-60=3$).

**Class size $=3$.**
